about: Parallels between the books, chosen by a person. Two sources: (1) 'model, reviewed': the search model proposed candidate pairs (each verse's closest verse in another book); a person read every candidate and kept only real parallels in story or teaching, wrote the one-line note and chose the theme; (2) 'hand-listed': known parallels from evals/search_parallels.json, each read and kept or left out. Pairs with threatening or theologically contentious verses are left out, and each verse is in at most one pair. 'score' is the model's similarity for the pair.

pairs.idea: Pharaoh's dream of seven fat and seven lean cows and seven ears of corn, which Joseph explains.

verses.text: The seven good kine are seven years; and the seven good ears are seven years: the dream is one.

And the king said: Lo! I saw in a dream seven fat kine which seven lean were eating, and seven green ears of corn and other (seven) dry. O notables! Expound for me my vision, if ye can interpret dreams.

pairs.idea: Joseph's dream of the sun, the moon and eleven stars bowing to him.

verses.text: And he dreamed yet another dream, and told it his brethren, and said, Behold, I have dreamed a dream more; and, behold, the sun and the moon and the eleven stars made obeisance to me.
When Joseph said unto his father: O my father! Lo! I saw in a dream eleven planets and the sun and the moon, I saw them prostrating themselves unto me.

pairs.idea: John and Elijah (Elias) named among the prophets.

verses.text: And they answered, John the Baptist: but some say, Elias; and others, One of the prophets.
And Zachariah and John and Jesus and Elias. Each one (of them) was of the righteous.

pairs.idea: The God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, the God of the fathers.

verses.text: That they may believe that the LORD God of their fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, hath appeared unto thee.

Or were ye present when death came to Jacob, when he said unto his sons: What will ye worship after me? They said: We shall worship thy god, the god of thy fathers, Abraham and Ishmael and Isaac, One Allah, and unto Him we have surrendered.

pairs.idea: Jonah swallowed by the fish.

verses.text: Now the LORD had prepared a great fish to swallow up Jonah. And Jonah was in the belly of the fish three days and three nights.
And the fish swallowed him while he was blameworthy;

pairs.idea: Pharaoh's army is drowned in the sea.

verses.text: Pharaoh's chariots and his host hath he cast into the sea: his chosen captains also are drowned in the Red sea.
And leave the sea behind at rest, for lo! they are a drowned host.

pairs.idea: The daughters of the priest of Midian come to water their father's flock, and Moses helps them (seven daughters in Exodus, two women in the Quran).

verses.text: Now the priest of Midian had seven daughters: and they came and drew water, and filled the troughs to water their father's flock.

And when he came unto the water of Midian he found there a whole tribe of men, watering. And he found apart from them two women keeping back (their flocks). He said: What aileth you? The two said: We cannot give (our flocks) to drink till the shepherds return from the water; and our father is a very old man.

pairs.idea: The angel tells Mary she will bear a son.

verses.text: And the angel said unto her, Fear not, Mary: for thou hast found favour with God.

(And remember) when the angels said: O Mary! Lo! Allah giveth thee glad tidings of a word from him, whose name is the Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary, illustrious in the world and the Hereafter, and one of those brought near (unto Allah).

pairs.idea: Moses' staff becomes a serpent.

verses.text: And he said, Cast it on the ground. And he cast it on the ground, and it became a serpent; and Moses fled from before it.
So he cast it down, and lo! it was a serpent, gliding.

pairs.idea: Joseph's brothers throw him into a pit/well.

verses.text: And they took him, and cast him into a pit: and the pit was empty, there was no water in it.
Then, when they led him off, and were of one mind that they should place him in the depth of the pit, We inspired in him: Thou wilt tell them of this deed of theirs when they know (thee) not.

pairs.idea: Zechariah is promised a son in old age.

verses.text: But the angel said unto him, Fear not, Zacharias: for thy prayer is heard; and thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son, and thou shalt call his name John.
(It was said unto him): O Zachariah! Lo! We bring thee tidings of a son whose name is John; we have given the same name to none before (him).

pairs.idea: Manna and quails in the wilderness.

verses.text: And it came to pass, that at even the quails came up, and covered the camp: and in the morning the dew lay round about the host.

And We caused the white cloud to overshadow you and sent down on you the manna and the quails, (saying): Eat of the good things wherewith We have provided you- they wronged Us not, but they did wrong themselves.

pairs.idea: Messengers tell Abraham of a son; his wife laughs.

verses.text: And he said, I will certainly return unto thee according to the time of life; and, lo, Sarah thy wife shall have a son. And Sarah heard it in the tent door, which was behind him.
And his wife, standing by laughed when We gave her good tidings (of the birth) of Isaac, and, after Isaac, of Jacob.

pairs.idea: Heaven and earth created in six days.

verses.text: For in six days the LORD made heaven and earth, the sea, and all that in them is, and rested the seventh day: wherefore the LORD blessed the sabbath day, and hallowed it.

Lo! your Lord is Allah Who created the heavens and the earth in six Days, then mounted He the Throne. He covereth the night with the day, which is in haste to follow it, and hath made the sun and the moon and the stars subservient by His command. His verily is all creation and commandment. Blessed be Allah, the Lord of the Worlds!

pairs.idea: The golden calf.

verses.text: And he received them at their hand, and fashioned it with a graving tool, after he had made it a molten calf: and they said, These be thy gods, O Israel, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt.
Then he produced for them a calf, of saffron hue, which gave forth a lowing sound. And they cried: This is your god and the god of Moses, but he hath forgotten.

pairs.idea: Joseph makes himself known to his brothers.

verses.text: And Joseph said unto his brethren, Come near to me, I pray you. And they came near. And he said, I am Joseph your brother, whom ye sold into Egypt.

They said: Is it indeed thou who art Joseph? He said: I am Joseph and this is my brother. Allah hath shown us favour. Lo! he who wardeth off (evil) and endureth (findeth favour); for lo! Allah loseth not the wages of the kindly.

pairs.idea: The flood: fountains of the deep and windows of heaven.

verses.text: In the six hundredth year of Noah's life, in the second month, the seventeenth day of the month, the same day were all the fountains of the great deep broken up, and the windows of heaven were opened.
Then opened We the gates of heaven with pouring water

pairs.idea: Baby Moses set adrift and taken in by Pharaoh's house.

verses.text: And when she could not longer hide him, she took for him an ark of bulrushes, and daubed it with slime and with pitch, and put the child therein; and she laid it in the flags by the river's brink.

Saying: Throw him into the ark, and throw it into the river, then the river shall throw it on to the bank, and there an enemy to Me and an enemy to him shall take him. And I endued thee with love from Me that thou mightest be trained according to My will,

pairs.idea: Adam and his wife eat from the forbidden tree.

verses.text: And when the woman saw that the tree was good for food, and that it was pleasant to the eyes, and a tree to be desired to make one wise, she took of the fruit thereof, and did eat, and gave also unto her husband with her; and he did eat.

Thus did he lead them on with guile. And when they tasted of the tree their shame was manifest to them and they began to hide (by heaping) on themselves some of the leaves of the Garden. And their Lord called them, (saying): Did I not forbid you from that tree and tell you: Lo! Satan is an open enemy to you?

pairs.idea: The Queen of Sheba visits Solomon.

verses.text: And when the queen of Sheba heard of the fame of Solomon concerning the name of the LORD, she came to prove him with hard questions.
Lo! I found a woman ruling over them, and she hath been given (abundance) of all things, and hers is a mighty throne.

pairs.idea: Noah builds the ark.

verses.text: Make thee an ark of gopher wood; rooms shalt thou make in the ark, and shalt pitch it within and without with pitch.
Build the ship under Our eyes and by Our inspiration, and speak not unto Me on behalf of those who do wrong. Lo! they will be drowned.

pairs.idea: God made every kind of animal, each after its kind.

verses.text: And God made the beast of the earth after his kind, and cattle after their kind, and every thing that creepeth upon the earth after his kind: and God saw that it was good.

Allah hath created every animal of water. Of them is (a kind) that goeth upon its belly and (a kind) that goeth upon two legs and (a kind) that goeth upon four. Allah createth what He will. Lo! Allah is Able to do all things.

pairs.idea: Calming the wind and the sea: in Mark Jesus stills a storm; the Quran says God can calm the wind so ships lie still.

verses.text: And he arose, and rebuked the wind, and said unto the sea, Peace, be still. And the wind ceased, and there was a great calm.
If He will He calmeth the wind so that they keep still upon its surface - Lo! herein verily are signs for every steadfast grateful (heart)-

pairs.idea: A garden of Eden with flowing rivers: the first garden in Genesis, the gardens of the life to come in the Quran.

verses.text: And a river went out of Eden to water the garden; and from thence it was parted, and became into four heads.
Gardens of Eden underneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide for ever. That is the reward of him who groweth.

pairs.idea: God created human beings male and female.

verses.text: Male and female created he them; and blessed them, and called their name Adam, in the day when they were created.

Allah created you from dust, then from a little fluid, then He made you pairs (the male and female). No female beareth or bringeth forth save with His knowledge. And no-one groweth old who groweth old, nor is aught lessened of his life, but it is recorded in a Book, Lo! that is easy for Allah.

pairs.idea: The splendour of the sun and the light of the moon come from God.

verses.text: He it is Who appointed the sun a splendour and the moon a light, and measured for her stages, that ye might know the number of the years, and the reckoning. Allah created not (all) that save in truth. He detaileth the revelations for people who have knowledge.
That splendour issuing from the sun that enlighteneth the whole world, that which is in the moon and in fire, that splendour know as from Me.

pairs.idea: Remembering God's marvellous works and wonders.

verses.text: Remember his marvellous works that he hath done, his wonders, and the judgments of his mouth;
Remembering, remembering, also that most marvellous form of Hari, great is my wonder, O King. I rejoice, again and again.

pairs.idea: Give thanks and praise to God.

verses.text: I will give thee thanks in the great congregation: I will praise thee among much people.

And verily We gave Luqman wisdom, saying: Give thanks unto Allah; and whosoever giveth thanks, he giveth thanks for (the good of) his soul. And whosoever refuseth - Lo! Allah is Absolute, Owner of Praise.

pairs.idea: What is done for God in secret is rewarded.

verses.text: That thine alms may be in secret: and thy Father which seeth in secret himself shall reward thee openly.
Lo! those who fear their Lord in secret, theirs will be forgiveness and a great reward.

pairs.idea: Keep the covenant and the oath you made with God.

verses.text: That thou shouldest enter into covenant with the LORD thy God, and into his oath, which the LORD thy God maketh with thee this day:
Fulfil the covenant of Allah when ye have covenanted, and break not your oaths after the asseveration of them, and after ye have made Allah surety over you. Lo! Allah knoweth what ye do.

pairs.idea: Paying one's vows at the house of God.

verses.text: I will go into thy house with burnt offerings: I will pay thee my vows,
Then let them make an end of their unkemptness and pay their vows and go around the ancient House.

pairs.idea: Honouring God's offerings comes from devotion of the heart.

verses.text: That (is the command). And whoso magnifieth the offerings consecrated to Allah, it surely is from devotion of the hearts,
Always magnifying Me, strenuous, firm in vows, prostrating themselves before Me, they worship Me with devotion ever harmonised.

pairs.idea: Devote yourself to God completely.

verses.text: So remember the name of thy Lord and devote thyself with a complete devotion -
On Me fix thy mind, be devoted to Me; sacrifice to Me; prostrate thyself before Me; harmonised thus in the Self, thou shalt come unto Me, having Me as thy supreme goal.

pairs.idea: Prayer and almsgiving belong to a devout life.

verses.text: And hath made me blessed wheresoever I may be, and hath enjoined upon me prayer and almsgiving so long as I remain alive,
The Blessed Lord said: Fearlessness, cleanness of life, steadfastness in the Yoga of wisdom, almsgiving, self-restraint and sacrifice and study of the Scriptures, austerity and straightforwardness,

pairs.idea: God accepts the devotion, not the size of the offering.

verses.text: He who offereth to Me with devotion a leaf, a flower, a fruit, water, that I accept from the striving self, offered as it is with devotion.

Their flesh and their food reach not Allah, but the devotion from you reacheth Him. Thus have We made them subject unto you that ye may magnify Allah that He hath guided you. And give good tidings (O Muhammad) to the good.

pairs.idea: Whatever you eat or do, offer it to God.

verses.text: Whatsoever thou doest, whatsoever thou eatest, whatsoever thou offerest, whatsoever thou givest, whatsoever thou doest of austerity, O Kaunteya, do thou that as an offering unto Me.
Whether therefore ye eat, or drink, or whatsoever ye do, do all to the glory of God.

pairs.idea: God leads people out of darkness into light, along straight paths.

verses.text: And I will bring the blind by a way that they knew not; I will lead them in paths that they have not known: I will make darkness light before them, and crooked things straight. These things will I do unto them, and not forsake them.
Whereby Allah guideth him who seeketh His good pleasure unto paths of peace. He bringeth them out of darkness unto light by His decree, and guideth them unto a straight path.

pairs.idea: Something better than trade and profit: wisdom, in Proverbs; what God gives, in the Quran.

verses.text: For the merchandise of it is better than the merchandise of silver, and the gain thereof than fine gold.

But when they spy some merchandise or pastime they break away to it and leave thee standing. Say: That which Allah hath is better than pastime and than merchandise, and Allah is the Best of providers.

pairs.idea: No effort made toward God is ever lost.

verses.text: And whoso desireth the Hereafter and striveth for it with the effort necessary, being a believer; for such, their effort findeth favour (with their Lord).
In this there is no loss of effort, nor is there transgression. Even a little of this knowledge protects from great fear.

pairs.idea: Charity or faith as a seed that grows manifold.

verses.text: And other fell on good ground, and did yield fruit that sprang up and increased; and brought forth, some thirty, and some sixty, and some an hundred.

The likeness of those who spend their wealth in Allah's way is as the likeness of a grain which groweth seven ears, in every ear a hundred grains. Allah giveth increase manifold to whom He will. Allah is All-Embracing, All-Knowing.

pairs.idea: Do not grieve over loss or exult over gain.

verses.text: Taking as equal pleasure and pain, gain and loss, victory and defeat, gird thee for the battle; thus thou shalt not incur sin.
That ye grieve not for the sake of that which hath escaped you, nor yet exult because of that which hath been given. Allah loveth not all prideful boasters,

pairs.idea: God is near to those who come to him with a contrite heart.

verses.text: The LORD is nigh unto them that are of a broken heart; and saveth such as be of a contrite spirit.
Who feareth the Beneficent in secret and cometh with a contrite heart.

pairs.idea: God's understanding and form are infinite.

verses.text: Great is our Lord, and of great power: his understanding is infinite.
With mouths, eyes, arms, breasts multitudinous, I see Thee everywhere, unbounded Form. Beginning, middle, end, nor source of Thee, Infinite Lord, infinite Form, I find;

pairs.idea: Something greater dwells within a person: God in the believer, says 1 John; the Self beyond mind and reason, says the Gita.

verses.text: Ye are of God, little children, and have overcome them: because greater is he that is in you, than he that is in the world.
It is said that the senses are great; greater than the senses is the mind: greater than the mind is the Reason; but what is greater than the Reason, is He.

pairs.idea: Nothing in heaven or earth is hidden from God.

verses.text: Can any hide himself in secret places that I shall not see him? saith the LORD. Do not I fill heaven and earth? saith the LORD.
Our Lord! Lo! Thou knowest that which we hide and that which we proclaim. Nothing in the earth or in the heaven is hidden from Allah.

pairs.idea: God is light.

verses.text: This then is the message which we have heard of him, and declare unto you, that God is light, and in him is no darkness at all.

Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth. The similitude of His light is as a niche wherein is a lamp. The lamp is in a glass. The glass is as it were a shining star. (This lamp is) kindled from a blessed tree, an olive neither of the East nor of the West, whose oil would almost glow forth (of itself) though no fire touched it. Light upon light. Allah guideth unto His light whom He will. And Allah speaketh to mankind in allegories, for Allah is Knower of all things.

pairs.idea: God's mercy forgives all sins.

verses.text: Who forgiveth all thine iniquities; who healeth all thy diseases;
Say: O My slaves who have been prodigal to their own hurt! Despair not of the mercy of Allah, Who forgiveth all sins. Lo! He is the Forgiving, the Merciful.

pairs.idea: The one Father of all beings.

verses.text: In whatsoever wombs mortals are produced, O Kaunteya, the great Eternal is their womb, I their generating father.
Have we not all one father? hath not one God created us? why do we deal treacherously every man against his brother, by profaning the covenant of our fathers?

pairs.idea: God dwells in the heart / is near.

verses.text: The Lord dwelleth in the hearts of all beings, O Arjuna, by His illusive Power causing all beings to revolve, as though mounted on a potter's wheel.
We verily created man and We know what his soul whispereth to him, and We are nearer to him than his jugular vein.

themes.name: Death and the life to come

pairs.idea: The final abode needs no sun or moon: God himself is its light.

verses.text: And the city had no need of the sun, neither of the moon, to shine in it: for the glory of God did lighten it, and the Lamb is the light thereof.
Nor doth the sun lighten there, nor moon, nor fire; having gone thither they return not; that is My supreme abode.

pairs.idea: The resurrection of the dead.

verses.text: Now if Christ be preached that he rose from the dead, how say some among you that there is no resurrection of the dead?
Provision (made) for men; and therewith We quicken a dead land. Even so will be the resurrection of the dead.

pairs.idea: The hour will come when those in the graves are raised.

verses.text: Marvel not at this: for the hour is coming, in the which all that are in the graves shall hear his voice,
And because the Hour will come, there is no doubt thereof; and because Allah will raise those who are in the graves.

pairs.idea: Death is likened to sleep.

verses.text: Howbeit Jesus spake of his death: but they thought that he had spoken of taking of rest in sleep.

Allah receiveth (men's) souls at the time of their death, and that (soul) which dieth not (yet) in its sleep. He keepeth that (soul) for which He hath ordained death and dismisseth the rest till an appointed term. Lo! herein verily are portents for people who take thought.

pairs.idea: God's own shall never perish.

verses.text: And I give unto them eternal life; and they shall never perish, neither shall any man pluck them out of my hand.
Speedily he becometh dutiful and goeth to eternal peace; O Kaunteya, know thou for certain that My devotee perisheth never.

pairs.idea: The heavens rolled up like a scroll.

verses.text: And all the host of heaven shall be dissolved, and the heavens shall be rolled together as a scroll: and all their host shall fall down, as the leaf falleth off from the vine, and as a falling fig from the fig tree.
The Day when We shall roll up the heavens as a recorder rolleth up a written scroll. As We began the first creation, We shall repeat it. (It is) a promise (binding) upon Us. Lo! We are to perform it.

pairs.idea: Life is like grass that withers.

verses.text: As for man, his days are as grass: as a flower of the field, so he flourisheth.

And coin for them the similitude of the life of the world as water which We send down from the sky, and the vegetation of the earth mingleth with it and then becometh dry twigs that the winds scatter. Allah is able to do all things.

pairs.idea: Every soul will die.

verses.text: And as it is appointed unto men once to die, but after this the judgment:

Every soul will taste of death. And ye will be paid on the Day of Resurrection only that which ye have fairly earned. Whoso is removed from the Fire and is made to enter paradise, he indeed is triumphant. The life of this world is but comfort of illusion.

pairs.idea: The body as a garment or house the self leaves.

verses.text: As a man, casting off worn-out garments, taketh new ones, so the dweller in the body, casting off worn-out bodies, entereth into others that are new.
For we know that if our earthly house of this tabernacle were dissolved, we have a building of God, an house not made with hands, eternal in the heavens.

pairs.idea: Take the lower place at a gathering; you will be asked to go up higher.

verses.text: But when thou art bidden, go and sit down in the lowest room; that when he that bade thee cometh, he may say unto thee, Friend, go up higher: then shalt thou have worship in the presence of them that sit at meat with thee.

O ye who believe! when it is said unto you: Make room! in assemblies, then make room; Allah will make way for you (hereafter). And when it is said: Come up higher! go up higher; Allah will exalt those who believe among you, and those who have knowledge, to high ranks. Allah is informed of what ye do.

pairs.idea: Strangers and foreigners are not outsiders; treat all alike.

verses.text: Now therefore ye are no more strangers and foreigners, but fellowcitizens with the saints, and of the household of God;
He who regards impartially lovers, friends, and foes, strangers, neutrals, foreigners and relatives, also the righteous and unrighteous, he excelleth.

pairs.idea: The pride of thinking one's wealth is self-made.

verses.text: And thou say in thine heart, My power and the might of mine hand hath gotten me this wealth.
"This to-day by me hath been won, that purpose I shall gain; this wealth is mine already, and also this shall be mine in future.

pairs.idea: Restrain the self from desire.

verses.text: When, again, as a tortoise draws in on all sides its limbs, he withdraws his senses from the objects of sense, then is his understanding well poised.
But as for him who feared to stand before his Lord and restrained his soul from lust,

pairs.idea: Giving alms in secret.

verses.text: But when thou doest alms, let not thy left hand know what thy right hand doeth:
If ye publish your almsgiving, it is well, but if ye hide it and give it to the poor, it will be better for you, and will atone for some of your ill-deeds. Allah is Informed of what ye do.

pairs.idea: Give without expecting reward or thanks.

verses.text: That alms given to one who does nothing in return, believing that a gift ought to be made in a fit place and time to a worthy person, that alms is accounted pure.
(Saying): We feed you, for the sake of Allah only. We wish for no reward nor thanks from you;

pairs.idea: Treat friend and foe alike / love your enemies.

verses.text: Alike to foe and friend, and also in fame and ignominy, alike in cold and heat, pleasures and pains, destitute of attachment,
But I say unto you, Love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you, and pray for them which despitefully use you, and persecute you;

pairs.idea: Moderation in eating.

verses.text: Verily yoga is not for him who eateth too much, nor who abstaineth to excess, nor who is too much addicted to sleep, nor even to wakefulness, O Arjuna.
O Children of Adam! Look to your adornment at every place of worship, and eat and drink, but be not prodigal. Lo! He loveth not the prodigals.
